evidence.title: Performance regression in striptags
evidence.excerpt:
After the merge of this PR: https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/pull/413/changes the function `Markup.striptags` has become much slower for larger inputs, contrary to what has been suggested by this PR.  

This problem has been noticed after benchmarking with arbitrary large inputs: 


| Case                               | Regex µs | Current µs   | Speedup  |
|----------------------------------------|----------|--------------|----------|
| plaintext_no_tags_50k_words            | 2937.05  | 2795.78      | 0.95x ← current_implementation |
| html_entities_only_no_tags_5k               | 4843.

answer.answer:
Markup.striptags collects text into a list in a single pass to fix a performance regression caused by quadratic string manipulation [pr:522]. This approach ensures the function scales linearly with input size, whereas previous incremental removal methods were significantly slower on large inputs [issue:521, pr:522].

### What changed
The implementation was updated to use a single `while` loop that scans for tags using `str.find`, appends the text between tags to a list named `parts`, and joins them once at the end [code:src/markupsafe/__init__.py#L199-L238, pr:522]. This replaced a "naive" refactor that had attempted to remove regular expressions by incrementally removing blocks, which resulted in quadratic complexity [pr:413, pr:522].

### Why
The change was motivated by benchmarks showing that the previous incremental approach was up to 1000x slower than the original regex-based version for large inputs [issue:521]. While the maintainers wanted to avoid regex due to its own performance issues and deep call stacks, the initial replacement was inefficient because it performed repeated string manipulations [pr:522, issue:521]. The single-pass list-collection method matches the style used for other scanners in Werkzeug to provide better performance without using regex [pr:522].

fixes #521

Discussion:
- @davidism: Thanks. I've been getting rid of regex for parsing in general (except for small things), as it was leading to too many performance issues on its own. Status: merged on 2026-10-01.

The regex implementation was removed in #413 with no clear benchmarks and replaced by a version containing quadratic string manipulation that does not scale. Fixing the implementation by appending sub-strings to a list and by doing a single loop over the value.

fixes #521

Benchmarks in https://github.com/odoo/odoo/pull/257889

Discussion:
- @davidism: Thanks. I've been getting rid of regex for parsing in general (except for small things), as it was leading to too many performance issues on its own. My initial refactors here and in Werkzeug were a bit too naive, they did speed up normal input but had the same issues as the regex they replaced. I've updated this PR to match the styles I used for other scanners in Werkzeug.

Status: merged on 2024-01-19.

The regular expression method of finding anything between comment or tag marks can be slow on large input, especially if it doesn't contain an end mark. Instead, use some simple `str.find` calls to incrementally remove blocks. The code can be cleaned up in `main` by using `:=` assignment expressions.

evidence.title: Performance regression in striptags
evidence.excerpt:
After the merge of this PR: https://github.com/pallets/markupsafe/pull/413/changes the function `Markup.striptags` has become much slower for larger inputs, contrary to what has been suggested by this PR.  

This problem has been noticed after benchmarking with arbitrary large inputs: 


| Case                               | Regex µs | Current µs   | Speedup  |
|----------------------------------------|----------|--------------|----------|
| plaintext_no_tags_50k_words            | 2937.05  | 2795.78      | 0.95x ← current_implementation |
| html_entities_only_no_tags_5k               | 4843.
